articles.title: Salesforce Implements AI Spending Limits to Control Costs
articles.summary: The company's new policy allocates monthly token budgets for every role, allowing employees to focus their AI spend on high-priority tasks.
articles.content: Salesforce is taking steps to rein in its AI spending after some employees spent thousands of dollars per month on tokens last quarter. According to an internal memo viewed by this publication, the company's Chief Operating Officer Miguel Milano has implemented a new policy that allocates monthly token budgets for every role, allowing employees to focus their AI spend on high-priority tasks. The move reflects a common challenge faced by companies embracing AI technology - balancing cost control with employee empowerment. Other businesses have introduced similar spending limits in an effort to curb the rising costs of artificial intelligence. While Salesforce is setting AI budgets at the team level, rather than companywide, team leaders will be responsible for managing their groups' AI usage. The goal, as stated by a company spokesperson, is to ensure that AI investments deliver maximum impact for both business and customers. Salesforce has tested this new approach on one team with promising results, reporting that the group operated well under budget after just two months without any decline in productivity. The sales organization under President and Chief Revenue Officer Alexa Vignone will have a strict $1,000 monthly limit for technical roles, while non-technical employees like sellers are allocated just $100 per month for AI tokens. In contrast, the Customer Success team led by Jim Roth has a more modest budget of $500 per month for technical personnel, with non-technical staff receiving the same $100 allowance as their counterparts in other departments. Meanwhile, the Global Professional Services and Forward Deployed Engineering teams under Lori Steele are also subject to these new spending limits. Other companies have been experimenting with similar measures to control AI expenses, including Coinbase which has implemented weekly caps ranging from $500 to $5,000 based on employee roles and seniority. JPMorgan Chase, for instance, has introduced a monthly limit of $2,000 for some engineers using Anthropic's Claude Code. The company's CEO Marc Benioff had previously estimated that Salesforce would spend around $300 million on Anthropic tokens this year, primarily to develop coding agents. This new approach aims to focus AI spending on projects with the greatest impact for customers and the business, rather than simply encouraging adoption. To manage AI spending, Salesforce has introduced new budget limits for employees based on their roles within the company. Monthly token spend limits have been set at varying levels depending on an employee's role, with technical roles such as Alexa's Org Technical Roles allowed to spend up to $1,000 per month, while non-technical GTM/Seller Roles are capped at $100 per month. This new system aims to reduce the financial burden of AI spending, which had previously seen employees exceed their budgets by thousands of dollars each month. The company is now encouraging employees and their managers to work together to stay within allocated limits. As part of this initiative, leaders will be responsible for managing their team's budgets, much like they would with travel and entertainment expenses. The new AI budget guidelines specify that any request exceeding 3 times the individual limit will require approval from a more senior manager, namely Alexa, Jim, or Lori, who will also involve finance in the decision-making process. These higher-value requests are reviewed on a monthly basis to ensure they align with company goals and justify the additional expenditure through a clear return on investment justification. The increased budget will be valid for 90 days before being reassessed. This temporary allocation is intended to support ongoing projects, but it's not a long-term solution. A more comprehensive process is in development to better manage AI spend. As part of this interim setup, leaders are encouraged to track individual and team usage through the AI Spend Dashboard. They should review usage monthly to identify areas where costs can be optimized without compromising results. The memo advises employees to regularly review their AI budget usage to identify areas where costs can be optimized without sacrificing results. Visibility into pooled team spending will be provided for leaders in countries represented by the Works Council, allowing them to monitor and manage token allocation effectively. With visibility comes responsibility; while individual employee usage will not be directly visible to leaders, they are expected to work with their teams on developing best practices for token management. articles.title: Cardinal Claudio Gugerotti Visits Jerusalem Amid Ongoing Christian Challenges
articles.summary: Vatican Cardinal Claudio Gugerotti visited Jerusalem to show solidarity with local Christians amidst challenging times.
articles.content: Cardinal Claudio Gugerotti's visit to Jerusalem aimed at conveying Pope Leo XIV's presence amidst challenging times for Christians in the region. The Vatican cardinal oversees care of the Catholic faithful in the Holy Land and his visit was a significant gesture of solidarity with local Christians. Gugerotti's trip took place on Tuesday, marking an important moment in the ongoing efforts to support Christian communities. Gugerotti prayed before the Holy Edicule inside the Church of the Holy Sepulcher, a site considered sacred by Christians as it marks where Jesus is believed to have been buried and resurrected. The cardinal's prayer was part of a solemn ceremony that brought together leaders from various Christian denominations in Jerusalem. Incense filled the air as clergy wore traditional robes, highlighting the importance of unity among the different faith groups. The unique arrangement of worship space in the basilica dates back to the 19th century and has sometimes led to tense interactions between the different Christian denominations. However, on this occasion, leaders from various backgrounds came together in a show of solidarity. Gugerotti's presence was accompanied by other Christian leaders, all of whom participated in the procession through Jerusalem's Old City. As they walked through the narrow stone alleyways, rows of Franciscan friars and a large cross preceded Gugerotti, creating a sense of grandeur and importance. The ceremony inside the centuries-old church offered a moment of hope for Christians in the region, who have been facing difficult times. The Israeli-Palestinian conflict has been taking a toll on the region's Christian community, with rising incidents of harassment against clergy and faithful. A recent violent attack on a religious sister in April sent shockwaves across Israel, highlighting the vulnerability of those serving in the Holy Land. Sister Marie Reine, a Catholic nun who participated in the procession, acknowledged that her community is not always welcomed in the region. However, she emphasized that their presence can also be a source of peace and comfort for many. The visit comes at a sensitive time for Israel's Christian minority, with most being Palestinians who have faced intense rhetoric following Arab-led parties' historic gains in national elections last month. Neighboring Jordan is still reeling from the aftermath of an attack on a Greek Orthodox church that left nine worshippers dead during a service. Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem, expressed his hopes for the visit to confirm faith and hope among priests, families, and young people who are striving to build a future in the region. As tensions continue to rise in the Holy Land, many Christians are finding it increasingly difficult to stay put. For some families, like Andre Haddad's, the thought of leaving is simply not an option. "To be here is a vocation," he said, emphasizing that his family cannot just abandon their reality. The emigration of Christians from across the Holy Land has become a pressing concern for church and lay leaders alike. Many feel vulnerable to organized crime due to their minority status in Israel. Wadie Abunassar, a Catholic community leader from Haifa, believes the state provides little protection to its Christian citizens. "Because I'm another Arab," he said, highlighting the challenges faced by Christians in the region. Gugerotti's six-day visit is set to take him to several key locations, including Bethlehem, where he will pay his respects at the Basilica of the Nativity, a site of great significance for Christians who believe Jesus was born there. The town itself is situated in the occupied West Bank, where tensions between Palestinian Muslims and Israeli settlers are running high. The dwindling Christian minority in the area has been vocal about its concerns regarding growing violence from Israeli settlers. Gugerotti's visit to Bethlehem will undoubtedly be a poignant reminder of the challenges facing Christians in the region. His schedule also includes meetings with the leaders of the Greek Orthodox and Armenian churches in Jerusalem, who attended Tuesday's prayers. During his previous papal trip to the Middle East last fall, Pope Leo prayed for unity among Christians after over 1,000 years of division between Eastern and Western churches. The significance of this visit cannot be overstated, as it holds out hope for a brighter future for Christians in the Holy Land. The visit by Pope Leo's envoy has sparked renewed optimism among Christians in the Holy Land, who have long been subjected to persecution and marginalization. Gugerotti's public engagements do not include meetings with Israeli leaders, but his presence is still a significant gesture of support for the local Christian community. Leo's efforts to reach out to Jewish faith leaders since assuming office last year are seen as a promising development in interfaith relations. The Pope has publicly denounced rising antisemitism and called for an end to the conflict in Gaza, where displacement and war have caused immense suffering. This message of comfort and unity is precisely what Christians in the Holy Land need to hear right now. articles.title: Microbes thrive in toxic quarry environments
articles.summary: A geomicrobiologist is studying microbes at a quarry site to understand how they can contribute to addressing climate change.
articles.content: A quarry site may seem like an inhospitable environment, but appearances can be misleading. The barren landscape and exposed rock face hide millions of living microbes that thrive in conditions toxic to other life forms. Dr. Thomas Jones, a geomicrobiologist, has spent years studying these microorganisms at CSIRO, Australia's national science agency. His work focuses on identifying microbes already present in the quarry, which he then takes back to the lab for further research and experimentation. Jones's approach is to find existing microbial populations that can be used as starter cultures for his experiments. In other words, he seeks out microorganisms that are already adapted to their environment and could potentially contribute to addressing climate change. When collecting samples from the quarry site, Jones carefully gathers a small amount of material from the rock surface. This "smear may seem insignificant, but it holds great potential for understanding how microbes can be harnessed to mitigate environmental damage. The scale of microbial activity spans from the tiniest particles to the vast expanse of the planet itself. Geomicrobiologist Jones has spent his career studying the intricate relationships between microbes and minerals, seeking ways to harness these interactions for human benefit. Many of the processes he's studied have been crucial in shaping our planet over millions of years, with ancient microbial activities still influencing Earth's geology today. According to Jones, microbes have been removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere for an astonishing 3.5 billion years, a testament to their enduring impact on the environment. Stromatolites are a fascinating example of this phenomenon, formed by communities of photosynthetic microbes that extract carbon dioxide and lock it into calcium carbonate mineral layers, creating layered mounds that have been essential in producing Earth's early atmospheric oxygen. The intricate details of microbial interactions with minerals can be revealed using advanced imaging techniques such as scanning electron microscopes, which provide extraordinary surface detail. To further analyze the elemental composition of these samples, Jones employs X-ray fluorescence (XRF) mapping at ANSTO's Australian Synchrotron, allowing him to pinpoint specific elements within the mineral structures. For Jones, geomicrobiology is a creative pursuit that involves piecing together complex puzzles, much like painting a picture, he seeks to fill in gaps in understanding by identifying missing pieces of information that exist elsewhere. Microbes are ubiquitous and can thrive even in harsh environments such as neglected mine tailings dams, where water is highly acidic but still manage to survive. The pH scale is a crucial tool for measuring acidity, with pure water sitting at a neutral 7. But as one moves down the scale, each step becomes increasingly acidic, with lemon juice reaching a pH of 2 and stomach acid plummeting to around 1. In fact, some microbes can thrive in environments that would be hostile to most other forms of life, with acidity levels even dipping into negative numbers. This remarkable ability to adapt has left researchers like Jones in awe of the resilience of these tiny organisms. The sheer diversity and ubiquity of microbes have made them a valuable asset in the fight against climate change. By harnessing their power, scientists are discovering new ways to mitigate the effects of global warming. One such process is enhanced rock weathering, which involves crushing up basalt, a type of gray rock commonly used in road gravel and building sites, and spreading it across farmland. As the rock breaks down, it releases essential minerals that help lock carbon dioxide out of the air while neutralizing soil acidity. By accelerating this natural process, researchers aim to create a more stable form of carbon storage that can help combat climate change. Field trips by Jones yield diverse microbial communities that are more resilient to changing environments than lab-grown strains. These broad communities are then adjusted through careful manipulation of nutrients and acidity, allowing a specific group to flourish. Once an optimal mix is achieved, it's dubbed gold" in microbe form - the "Daddy consortium". This potent blend of microbes is now ready for deployment in the field. However, things don't always go according to plan when introducing these microbes into complex ecosystems like soil. Pure cultures accustomed to laboratory environments can struggle to adapt and may be outcompeted by established microbial populations. Every microbe in a given environment plays a vital role and has evolved to thrive under specific conditions, leaving little room for newcomers. Jones acknowledges that working on farms adds an extra layer of complexity due to the delicate balance already present. Any changes to soil chemistry could disrupt this equilibrium and undermine the efforts put into maintaining the farm's ecosystem. Jones must therefore be mindful of his approach when introducing microbes to these environments. When working with farms, timing is a crucial factor in deploying rock dust and microbes effectively. Applying them just after rain allows the microbes to settle and establish themselves before being washed away. Conversely, spreading them out just before the onset of the wet season enables them to be carried into the soil where they can take hold. Throughout this process, Jones remains acutely aware that he's working with living organisms that require careful consideration and handling. His approach must strike a balance between introducing beneficial microbes while respecting the existing ecosystem and minimizing potential disruptions. To succeed in enlisting microbes to combat climate change, it's essential that they are content and able to thrive in their new environment. This requires a delicate balance between providing them with what they need to function effectively and not overstimulating them. Jones' background is in geology, but he discovered his passion for microbiology through elective courses in college. It was there that he became aware of the vast potential of microbes to be harnessed for beneficial purposes. This epiphany marked a significant turning point in his academic and professional journey. The XXXX brewery in Brisbane proved to be an unexpected yet valuable source of starter cultures for Jones' early research. He has always been drawn to novel and unconventional approaches, which has served him well in his work as a microbiologist. His enthusiasm for the field is evident in his comments about its vast potential. Jones' professional path has taken him on a global journey, with stops in Australia, Brazil, and southern Africa. Along the way, he completed his Ph.D. at the University of Queensland and successfully scaled up microbial techniques from laboratory settings to industry applications. This experience has provided him with a unique perspective on the practical applications of microbiology. The work being conducted by Jones and his team is focused on developing mineral-building microbes that can store carbon for extended periods in Western Australia. In this context, he is collaborating with some of the oldest and most effective carbon catchers on Earth, the microbes themselves. He has a straightforward approach when working with these tiny helpers - he simply asks them to take on the task of capturing carbon from the atmosphere. The microbes are a massive team effort, comprising the vast majority of Earth's inhabitants, and most of them remain invisible to the naked eye. articles.title: Groundbreaking Discovery Made in Astrophysics Using NSF VLBA
articles.summary: A team led by Paul Boven made a surprising discovery that both stars in DG CVn emit detectable radio waves, allowing astronomers to track their individual motions with remarkable accuracy.
articles.content: Astronomers have made a groundbreaking discovery in the field of astrophysics by measuring the orbit, masses, and distance of a pair of small, active stars with unprecedented precision. The observations were made using the U.S. National Science Foundation's Very Long Baseline Array (NSF VLBA), operated by the National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NRAO). This binary system, known as DG CVn, is located approximately 59 light-years from Earth and consists of two red dwarf stars that orbit each other. A team led by Paul Boven, a network system engineer at the Joint Institute for Very Long Baseline Interferometry ERIC (JIVE), made the surprising discovery that both stars in DG CVn emit detectable radio waves. This allowed astronomers to track their individual motions across the sky with remarkable accuracy. The observations provide a detailed picture of this binary system, which is still relatively young, estimated to be between 30 and 150 million years old. DG CVn is an interesting case study for astronomers because it consists of two red dwarf stars that exhibit intense activity. When these stars rotate rapidly, they generate powerful magnetic fields and intense flares that produce strong radio and X-ray emission. This makes them a rare and fascinating subject of study in the field of astrophysics. The observations were made over an 18-year period, including new data collected between 2023 and 2025 using the NSF VLBA. By combining this data with previous observations, the team was able to determine the stars' orbit and masses with unusual accuracy. This achievement is a testament to the power of long-term observations in astronomy. The study's lead author, Paul Boven, is a Ph.D. student at Leiden Observatory and a network system engineer at JIVE. His team's work provides valuable insights into the behavior of red dwarf stars and their potential for intense activity. The findings have been published in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics, offering a new perspective on this fascinating binary system. Further research is needed to understand the complex dynamics of DG CVn and its implications for our understanding of star formation and evolution. The study's results also highlight the importance of continued observations using advanced astronomical instruments like the NSF VLBA. The system's radio emission has been found to surge dramatically following powerful X-ray outbursts, leaving astronomers with a pressing question: which star is responsible for this phenomenon? The researchers' initial observations of DG CVn were motivated by a search for planets around nearby stars. However, the system's behavior proved far more complex than anticipated, exhibiting large and unpredictable motion that defied explanation. We were fortunate to have developed the necessary tools to interpret these motions, said Boven, but the real surprise came when we detected a second radio-loud dwarf during our confirmation observations. The team combined archival data from 2007-2010 with seven new observing sessions between 2023 and 2025 to produce 27 precise measurements of the system's two stars. The team used the NSF VLBA's unique capability to combine the signals from its 10 radio telescopes across North America into a single, highly sensitive instrument. This allowed them to pinpoint the locations of the radio emission from each star with unprecedented precision. DG CVn is an exemplary case of what can be achieved through precise radio astrometry, according to Jay Blanchard, an astronomer at the NSF NRAO and co-author on the study. By tracking the two stars over many years, researchers can observe their orbital motion directly and use that information to determine properties that would otherwise be extremely challenging to measure. The observations revealed that the two stars orbit each other once every 4.511 years in a stretched, elliptical path. At their closest approach, they come within about 0.59 times the average distance between Earth and the sun. DG CVn A is significantly more massive than DG CVn B, with approximately 39% of the sun's mass, while its companion has roughly 36%. These masses were determined using data from the team's observations. The system is relatively close to Earth, situated at a distance of about 59.3 light-years away. Researchers employed a technique called parallax to calculate this distance by measuring the tiny apparent shift in the position of DG CVn as Earth moves around the sun. Knowing both the system's distance and the way the two stars move around each other enabled the researchers to calculate their masses with exceptional accuracy, providing one of the most precise dynamical measurements yet for a binary system of this type. The gravitational interactions between two stars in a binary system can have far-reaching consequences for their planetary systems. The close proximity of the stars in DG CVn, just 0.59 astronomical units apart, would have limited the size of the gas and dust disks surrounding each star as they formed. This limitation likely had an impact on the formation of planets around these stars. To remain stable, a planet orbiting one of the stars would need to complete its orbit in under 23 days. Conversely, a planet that orbited both stars would require a much longer orbital period, lasting at least 36 years. The constraints on planetary orbits imposed by the binary system provide valuable insights into how such systems can influence the formation and survival of planets. The close encounters between the two stars may have also played a role in shaping their planetary systems. VLBI, or very long baseline interferometry, proved to be an essential tool for this research. By combining radio telescopes over vast distances, researchers were able to make extremely precise measurements of the binary system's position and motion. The exceptional precision achieved through VLBI enabled the researchers to calculate the masses of the stars with great accuracy. articles.title: Flock Safety Cameras Found in Public Spaces Across US
articles.summary: Flock Safety cameras are often overlooked despite their widespread presence in public areas.
articles.content: Flock cameras have become ubiquitous in public spaces, but their presence often goes unnoticed. Their capabilities and potential uses far exceed what most people assume they can do. The automated license plate reader (ALPR) version is perhaps the most well-known type, typically mounted on a pole with a solar panel attached for power. However, Flock Safety's product has become synonymous with ALPR cameras, despite there being numerous other manufacturers and vendors offering similar technology. These alternative products often have distinct designs but serve essentially the same purpose: reading license plates and recording vehicle activity. Most of these devices are small, roughly hand-sized, and have a vertically oval shape, making them easy to miss in their surroundings. A solar panel is frequently attached to provide power, ensuring continuous operation without interruption. The appearance of ALPR cameras can vary significantly depending on the manufacturer, with some notable examples being those made by Leonardo and Genetec. Flock cameras blend in seamlessly with their surroundings, making them easily mistaken for standard traffic cameras or vice versa. This blurring of lines creates a challenge for projects like DeFlock, which relies on volunteers to visually identify Flock cameras. The capabilities of Flock cameras extend beyond automatic license plate recognition (ALPRs). Depending on the customer's requirements, the system can capture additional details such as roof racks on vehicles and bumper stickers. Some setups even come equipped with microphones, while others can recognize specific clothing items or facial features like beards. Flock cameras are typically deployed in high-traffic areas where roads converge, often mounted on poles at busy intersections or neighborhood entrances. Given the significant presence of homeowners associations (HOAs) among Flock's customer base, it's not surprising to find them at these locations. Shopping centers also represent potential sites for Flock camera installations. When attempting to identify a Flock camera, its orientation is an important consideration. Since the primary purpose is to capture license plates, the camera should be angled accordingly. A telltale sign of a Flock camera is the presence of the company's bird logo on the device and a solar panel above it, typically indicating self-sufficiency. The lack of additional equipment nearby often serves as another indicator that a camera is a Flock model. In contrast to red light and speed cameras, which are usually larger and connected to traffic signals or enforcement poles, Flock cameras tend to be more discreet. Flock cameras come in various forms, not all of which are immediately recognizable as such. The company offers a range of products, including the Condor, a spherical camera that can rotate 360 degrees to track individuals. This particular model is typically mounted near high-traffic areas where pedestrians congregate. However, Flock's product line extends beyond fixed installations, also encompassing mobile security trailers and gunshot detection systems. The company has even explored drone-based solutions for emergency response situations. As a result of this proliferation of different products, it may become increasingly challenging to identify a Flock camera or one similar in design. This can be attributed to the growing trend of repurposing standard IP cameras as plate readers using video integration tools. Consequently, users will need to rely on more comprehensive resources to determine whether law enforcement agencies are utilizing such technology in their area. A useful starting point for this inquiry is the Atlas of Surveillance, a searchable database maintained by the Electronic Frontier Foundation that catalogues the surveillance technologies employed by various law enforcement agencies. To uncover the presence of Flock cameras in your area, it's essential to be proactive in seeking out information. Submitting a public records request is one effective way to obtain this data, allowing you to access detailed information about these surveillance systems. A more hands-on approach involves attending local council meetings or asking business owners and homeowners' associations directly if they are aware of any Flock cameras in the area. articles.title: GM President Confident in Detroit's Automotive Industry Amid Chinese Competition
articles.summary: General Motors President Mark Reuss asserted his confidence in Detroit's automotive industry at the F500 Innovation Forum, stating "I'm not afraid of Chinese cars." However, he also...
articles.content: General Motors President Mark Reuss asserted his confidence in Detroit's automotive industry at the F500 Innovation Forum, stating "I'm not afraid of Chinese cars." However, he also acknowledged that GM is closely monitoring China's rapidly growing manufacturing sector. China has set a remarkable record for auto exports, shipping over 8 million passenger vehicles during the first 10 months of 2026. To counter this trend, Reuss highlighted the strengths of Detroit's GM factories, emphasizing their capacity to produce high-quality vehicles at scale. Reuss' comments were made during a panel discussion with Fortune's Executive Editor Lee Clifford, where he showcased GM's expertise in critical areas such as safety, durability, and long-term reliability. He also emphasized the importance of design, stating "aesthetic design is an essential aspect of the company's products. The stakes are high for American workers, who make up a significant portion of the motor vehicles and component parts sector. According to the Department of Energy, this industry employed around 2.6 million U.S. workers in 2025, a decrease of over 50,000 from the previous year. Reuss pointed to GM's factories as a key competitive advantage, citing their ability to produce at scale and maintain a large workforce. He also emphasized the importance of talent, stating our people are second to none and asserting that GM has the best automotive expertise in the country. GM's president, Reuss, emphasized that the company has been studying its competitors in China since 1984, having operated there for nearly four decades. This experience has given them a deep understanding of Chinese cars and their capabilities. As he noted, We know Chinese cars, which suggests that GM is well-positioned to compete with its Chinese rivals. GM's approach to staying ahead of the competition involves not just studying its local competitors but also those from around the world. According to Reuss, the company disassembles rival vehicles to gain insights into their design and technology. This hands-on approach allows them to learn from others and adapt their own strategies accordingly. As he quipped, Only the paranoid survive, right? China's auto export growth has been nothing short of remarkable, with the country shipping over eight million passenger vehicles in the first ten months of 2026 alone. In October, exports reached a staggering 927,000 units, representing a 62.3% increase from the previous year. This surge is part of an already record-breaking year for Chinese auto exports. China's electric vehicle production has been driving much of this growth, with the country accounting for nearly three-quarters of global EV production in 2025. That year, China produced around 16 million electric cars, and its exports more than doubled to a record 2.5 million vehicles. These figures represent over one-third of all Chinese vehicle exports and demonstrate the significant role that electric vehicles are playing in driving the country's auto export boom. The automotive sector plays a significant role in the US manufacturing base, supporting millions of jobs across various industries including factories, suppliers, distribution networks, and repair businesses. According to a report by the Congressional Research Service released in March 2026, the automotive industry accounts for approximately 4.8% of the country's GDP and supports around 10.1 million direct and indirect employment opportunities. This sector is crucial to the US economy, providing a substantial contribution to its overall growth. General Motors has been working on making its vehicles more affordable by pricing six models at around $30,000, with over 600,000 units sold so far this year following nearly one million last year. The company's president emphasized that achieving profitability in such a competitive market is challenging but they are committed to succeeding. GM learned the hard way that cutting costs alone cannot solve problems; instead, the company went through several reorganizations, downsizing, and consolidations over the years. This experience culminated in the company filing for bankruptcy in 2009, with its president noting that nothing happens until you sell a car." GM's domestic manufacturing footprint is being strengthened through significant investments in supply chains, production capacity, and final assembly facilities within the US. This move aims to bolster America's ability to manufacture vehicles and technology, which Reuss believes is crucial for its long-term competitive success. He emphasizes that bringing industrial might and jobs back into the country will have a profound impact on its economic landscape. Reuss advocates for a single national rulebook instead of state-by-state regulation, citing the billions of dollars wasted by the industry trying to comply with individual state regulations rather than a consistent nationwide set of rules. The demand for gas-powered engines remains high and is expected to persist in the coming years. articles.title: England's NEET Crisis Affects Almost 1 Million Young People Between Ages 16-24
articles.summary: A landmark review by Alan Milburn has led to Prime Minister Andy Burnham adopting a "whole-childhood approach" to prevent young people from becoming NEET.
articles.content: Almost 1 million young people in England between the ages of 16 and 24 are not in education, employment, or training, sparking concerns about the country's NEET crisis. In response to a landmark review on this issue by Alan Milburn, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has vowed to adopt a "whole-childhood approach" aimed at preventing young people from falling through the cracks. This means providing support to those with specific needs and vulnerabilities. Research shows that poverty, poor mental health, and special education needs or disabilities are common among NEET individuals. However, even when multiple risk factors are present in two young people, their paths can diverge significantly, with one moving into further education or employment while the other becomes NEET. Despite being able to identify patterns of disadvantage through data analysis, there's a significant gap between understanding which young people are at risk and knowing what contributes to them becoming or remaining NEET. The distinction between identifying risk and understanding pathways to becoming NEET is crucial for effective policy-making. While researchers have made significant progress in pinpointing which young people are most likely to end up not in education, employment, or training (NEET), the underlying reasons remain shrouded in mystery. Our team reviewed 861 records and identified 36 relevant data sets that shed light on NEET levels among 16- to 24-year-olds in England. These data sets include national studies like the Millennium Cohort Study and large household surveys such as Understanding Society, which provide a comprehensive picture of young people's circumstances and outcomes. In addition to these studies, we also examined records from schools, government departments, and other public services that collect data on young people's lives over time. While only four of the 36 identified data sets measured NEET status directly, others included valuable information about groups at greater risk of becoming NEET and how their lives changed over time. The available data offer a nuanced understanding of patterns and characteristics that help policymakers identify who may require additional support. However, our review revealed a significant gap: while data can pinpoint which young people are at risk of becoming NEET, they often fail to explain why individuals' pathways diverge in the first place. A typical data set might reveal correlations between school absence and disengagement from education, employment, or training, but it usually cannot provide insight into what happens between those two points in time. This gap highlights a critical challenge for policymakers seeking to address the NEET problem effectively. Administrative records often fall short in answering crucial questions about a young person's life. For instance, were their support needs recognized and addressed during a critical transition period? The lack of information on these matters hinders policymakers' efforts to address the NEET problem effectively. Our previous research has shown that accessing linked administrative data is a significant challenge. This gap highlights the limitations of relying solely on administrative records to understand the complexities of youth transitions. Young people with special education needs and disabilities (Send) are around twice as likely to become NEET as those without such needs, according to our analysis. The presence of childhood poverty further exacerbates this risk. Among young men eligible for free school meals due to their family's low income and also having a Send record, nearly one in four were NEET, compared with fewer than one in 14 among those with neither characteristic. Analyzing youth disengagement in England is a complex task that requires more than just identifying at-risk groups. One key challenge is understanding the context surrounding these young people's experiences. Administrative records can provide valuable insights into patterns and trends, but they often fail to capture the intricate web of factors influencing an individual's path. Young people's own perspectives are crucial in filling this knowledge gap. Through interviews, participatory research, and accessible surveys, researchers can gain a deeper understanding of how educational experiences, local opportunities, family responsibilities, and support systems interact. This approach allows for a more nuanced understanding of the challenges faced by young people. The government-commissioned review on youth unemployment highlights the importance of shifting the narrative away from individual failing. The research suggests that even when we identify high-risk groups, we may not have the evidence needed to understand where support breaks down and what works in these situations. This gap in knowledge hinders the development of effective strategies for addressing youth disengagement. A coordinated system tackling youth disengagement must move beyond mere identification of at-risk individuals. It demands a deeper understanding of the barriers young people encounter, as well as the support that helps them transition towards education, training, or employment. This requires learning from their experiences and using this knowledge to inform policy decisions. Effective interventions rely on more than just administrative data; they also require an empathetic understanding of the challenges faced by young people. By prioritizing these perspectives and experiences, policymakers can develop targeted strategies that address the root causes of youth disengagement, rather than just its symptoms. By analyzing administrative and research data, England has been able to identify which young people are at risk of becoming Not in Education, Employment, or Training (NEET). However, this information does not provide a clear understanding of why these individuals are more likely to be NEET. To address the root causes of youth disengagement, policymakers need to go beyond just identifying the problem. This involves considering various factors that may contribute to a young person's likelihood of becoming NEET. As Lombardo et al. point out in their research, administrative and research data can only provide part of the picture, and other perspectives are essential for developing effective strategies. Understanding why certain groups of young people are more likely to be NEET is crucial for policymakers to develop targeted interventions that address the underlying causes of disengagement. By prioritizing these perspectives and experiences, policymakers can create a more comprehensive approach to addressing youth disengagement, ultimately helping to reduce the number of young people who become NEET in England. articles.title: EU and ASEAN Mark 50 Years of Diplomatic Ties Amid Trade Agreement Progress

articles.content: The European Union and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) are on the cusp of significant developments in their trade relations, as they mark 50 years of diplomatic ties next year. A major milestone will be the implementation of a long-awaited trade agreement with Indonesia, while negotiations with Thailand and Malaysia are gaining momentum. The EU is also close to finalizing a deal with the Philippines, which could bring the number of Southeast Asian states with which it has trade agreements up from just two today to six by the end of next year. The anniversary of their diplomatic ties may also revive the long-held ambition of a broader trade agreement between the EU and ASEAN. This would represent a significant step forward in their economic cooperation, but several challenges must first be overcome. On November 17, the European Commission hosted a dialogue in Brussels to discuss trade relations with Southeast Asia, where progress on existing and pending free trade agreements (FTAs) was assessed. The European Union's push for deeper trade ties with Southeast Asia has made significant progress in recent years, but experts warn that informal barriers to commerce still pose a major challenge. To truly succeed, free trade agreements (FTAs) need to address not only formal regulations, but also the unwritten rules and local practices that can be just as daunting for European businesses. For instance, European companies with limited experience in Southeast Asia would greatly benefit from on-the-ground support, particularly practical guidance on navigating informal business customs and local regulations. This could involve expanding assistance offered by European chambers of commerce, trade delegations, and EU offices in the region to help firms find distributors, explain licensing requirements, and qualify for preferential tariffs. Regular consultations between Brussels and businesses in Southeast Asia could help identify potential trade issues early on, preventing them from escalating into full-blown disputes. The EU's trade policy has taken on a new dimension, driven by a desire to reduce strategic dependencies. According to Nessel, this means setting clear objectives for trade policy, which is currently lacking. One area of concern is the EU's reliance on a small number of suppliers for critical minerals used in clean technologies. Southeast Asian producers, such as Indonesia, want foreign investors to help develop domestic processing industries rather than simply exporting raw materials. The EU and Indonesia have already clashed over Jakarta's restrictions on nickel exports. European investment in processing facilities, environmental agreements, and regulatory clarity would provide tangible benefits to both sides. Nessel emphasized that the true value of a free trade agreement lies not only in opening up new markets but also in giving the EU leverage to maintain access to those markets. The European Union is reevaluating its approach to trade agreements in Southeast Asia, a region where informal barriers often hinder business operations. Indonesia's decision to terminate bilateral investment treaties with several EU countries, including the Netherlands and Spain, has sparked concerns about the lack of legal protections for investors in the country. This development highlights the need for clearer guidelines on investments in Indonesia, a key player in Southeast Asia. The EU is reassessing its strategy for trade agreements in ASEAN, considering whether to pursue bilateral deals or revive its original ambition of a region-to-region agreement with ASEAN. ASEAN has already established regional free trade agreements with several economies, including China, which upgraded its deal with the bloc in October 2025. This development underscores the complexity of the EU's efforts to establish deeper ties with ASEAN through trade agreements. The EU-ASEAN Business Council is advocating for negotiations on a region-to-region Digital Trade Agreement and Investment Protection Agreement, citing the need for common approaches to customs procedures, supply-chain standards, and green technologies. The EU-ASEAN Business Council is pushing for a region-to-region Digital Trade Agreement and Investment Protection Agreement, highlighting the need for standardization in customs procedures and supply-chain management as key obstacles to deeper trade ties. A convenient deadline of 2027 has been set for agreeing on what comes next, but some warn against mistaking diplomatic ceremony for actual progress. articles.title: Groundbreaking Discovery Made at CERN Using Large Hadron Collider
articles.summary: Physicists at CERN have made a groundbreaking discovery using the Large Hadron Collider, gaining insight into the universe's behavior at an unprecedented scale.
articles.content: Physicists at CERN have made a groundbreaking discovery using the Large Hadron Collider, gaining insight into the universe's behavior at an unprecedented scale. The research explores the "zeptoverse, a realm where particles interact within less than a hundred-trillionth of a wavelength of visible light. This tiny scale is the smallest yet investigated by scientists. The study may hold the key to solving long-standing cosmic enigmas, such as the abundance of matter over antimatter in the universe and the nature of dark matter that accounts for 85% of all matter. Researchers announced their findings at a seminar on November 3 at CERN, where they operate the LHC particle accelerator. Located near Geneva on the border between France and Switzerland, the LHC is the world's largest particle accelerator. Physicists were studying elusive beauty quarks, subatomic particles related to the standard up" and "down quarks found in atomic cores. When these particles are created through high-speed collisions at the LHC, they decay rapidly. The study has not undergone peer review yet, appearing as a preprint. Beauty quarks live for only one and a half trillionths of a second before decaying, making them challenging to detect and study. Physicists at CERN are exploring a previously uncharted territory known as the 'zeptoverse', where new particles and forces may be hiding in plain sight. This realm is characterized by incredibly small scales, measured in zeptometers - trillionths of a nanometer. By analyzing rare forms of beauty-quark decay, researchers hope to uncover anomalies that could reveal new physics at work. The process involves studying the breakdown of beauty quarks, which have a very short lifespan and are notoriously difficult to detect. Researchers believe that by examining these decays in detail, they may be able to identify patterns or outcomes that don't fit with current understanding. If successful, this approach could lead to groundbreaking discoveries about the fundamental nature of matter. Scientists are optimistic that their efforts will pay off, citing the potential for new particles to explain long-standing mysteries such as dark matter and the existence of matter in the universe. The 'zeptoverse' offers a unique window into these phenomena, allowing researchers to probe scales that were previously inaccessible. By exploring this uncharted territory, scientists hope to shed light on some of the biggest questions in physics. Physicists are now able to collect data at an unprecedented rate, thanks to advances in technology and computing power. According to particle physicist Harry Cliff, We're now recording in a single year what took 10 years to record in the past. This accelerated pace has enabled researchers to uncover evidence of rare beauty-quark decays, a major breakthrough after decades of searching. The B0 to mu+ mu− decay is an extremely rare occurrence in the world of particle physics, happening only once in 10 billion beauty particles. This form of decay involves a beauty quark colliding with its oppositely charged counterpart, resulting in the annihilation of both particles and the creation of a pair of smaller particles: a muon and an antimuon. The process is highly complex and requires specific conditions to occur, which made it difficult for researchers to detect until now. A major experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) called LHCb was specifically designed to study beauty quarks in more detail. The 2024 upgrade of LHCb enabled the detection of different types of particles with greater precision. The researchers employed machine learning techniques to suppress a massive amount of background noise, allowing them to detect the first evidence of B0 to mu+ mu− decay. This breakthrough is significant because it allows scientists to better understand the behavior of beauty quarks and their interactions. Physicists at CERN have made a groundbreaking discovery that allows them to study the universe at an unprecedented scale, entering what's being called the zeptoverse". This achievement is particularly significant as it enables researchers to gain insights into the behavior of beauty quarks and their interactions. The team's next step is to upgrade the LHCb experiment to fully leverage improvements in the Large Hadron Collider's luminosity scheduled for the 2030s. However, the project has faced financial setbacks in recent times, with some funding being withdrawn. Despite these challenges, researchers remain optimistic about the prospects of collecting and analyzing data from this cutting-edge experiment. The prospect of exploring the zeptoverse is exciting, as it offers a unique opportunity to probe distances that are unimaginably small. With hundreds of decays expected to be collected in the future, scientists will be able to make precise measurements and gain a deeper understanding of the behavior of beauty quarks at these tiny scales. articles.title: Federal Judge Keeps Most Records Related to Rep. Ilhan Omar Investigation Sealed
articles.summary: A federal judge has ruled that most records related to an investigation into Rep. Ilhan Omar's home will remain sealed, but a specific exchange about protecting her speech and debate rights can be made public.
articles.content: A federal judge has made a ruling on the release of certain records related to an investigation into Rep. Ilhan Omar's home. Chief Judge James E. Boasberg agreed with the Justice Department that most of the search warrant affidavit should remain sealed. However, the judge believes that a specific exchange between attorneys and a federal magistrate judge about protecting the lawmaker's "speech and debate rights is worthy of being made public. This exchange involves discussions on how to safeguard Omar's freedom to express herself without fear of repercussions. The speech and debate clause of the Constitution was cited in this context, which aims to preserve the independence of the legislative branch by ensuring that lawmakers are not questioned or held accountable for their words outside of Congress. A federal magistrate judge has put protocols in place to protect Rep. Ilhan Omar's rights as a member of Congress during an ongoing investigation into her activities. The search warrant for Omar's home was authorized by Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh, who took steps to safeguard the congresswoman's privileges despite the unusual overt investigative action against a sitting member of Congress just weeks after the election. Omar's phone was seized as part of the search, and the Justice Department is still reviewing materials taken from her home, with one attorney acknowledging that some information could be unsealed about discussions related to speech and debate. The investigation into Rep. Ilhan Omar's home revolves around potential immigration-related crimes, according to people familiar with the probe. This aspect of the case has been publicly acknowledged by high-ranking officials, including Vice President JD Vance and President Donald Trump. Vice President Vance had earlier stated that he believes Rep. Omar definitely committed immigration fraud", specifically pointing to this type of crime as the focus of the investigation. Boasberg noted that even if officials were trying to downplay their involvement, public statements from those in positions of authority can be difficult to ignore. The judge's comments suggest that some information may eventually be made public about Rep. Omar's case, potentially shedding light on the specifics surrounding her immigration history and any potential wrongdoing. articles.title: Gift-Giving Ideas from Vogue Editors
articles.summary: Vogue editors share their unique gift ideas for the holiday season, including festive items and practical presents.
articles.content: Gift-giving can be an overwhelming task, especially when trying to find something unique and thoughtful for loved ones. For those who struggle with finding inspiration, being part of a team that surrounds you with great taste and shopping expertise is a major advantage. As a member of the Vogue Shopping team, I've honed my gift-giving skills over the years, gaining insight into what makes an exceptional present beyond the basics. I polled our offices to gather ideas from colleagues on what they plan to gift this holiday season, covering every type of person on your list. Chloe Malle, head of editorial content, is a self-proclaimed Christmas enthusiast who loves gifting festive items and receiving them in return. She's particularly fond of peppermint striped tapers from House & Parties, festive Liberty print holiday crowns, and Nutcracker crackers, planning to get these for herself and others as gifts. These small yet thoughtful gestures are perfect for adding a touch of festivity to any occasion. As the holiday season approaches, Vogue editors are sharing their gift-giving secrets, and it's clear that they value thoughtful gestures over expensive presents. For smaller gifts, such as hostess presents or treats for weekend visitors, Elly Leavitt, lifestyle shopping editor, relies on a few well-chosen items. A beautiful soap is always a welcome addition to any gathering, while a pair of nice gardening gloves is a practical and appreciated gift for those who enjoy tending to their garden. A more unique approach to gifting can be seen in the lasagna parties hosted by Leavitt every December. Each guest receives a tiny ornament that doubles as a wine glass charm, adding a personal touch to the evening's festivities. Talia Abbas, shopping director, is an avid enthusiast of food-related gifts, which she believes are both meaningful and practical. For her, the perfect gift is one that can be kept in the kitchen, such as a specialty olive oil or a beautifully crafted jar of mustard. Incense papers are another favorite gift-giving item for Abbas, who enjoys pairing them with tea and taralli for a thoughtful and indulgent treat. These small gestures may not break the bank, but they make a lasting impression on those who receive them. Madeline Fass, fashion market director, is particularly fond of luxurious scents, which she believes evoke a sense of relaxation and tranquility. Two fragrances from Flamingo Estate stand out to her as exceptional choices for gift-giving. Fass also appreciates the elegance of Officine Universelle Buly's packaging, which eliminates the need for wrapping or additional presentation. This is especially convenient for those who need to travel with their gifts, ensuring that they arrive at their destination looking polished and refined. As the holiday season approaches, Vogue editors are sharing their gift ideas for friends and family. For some, gifting is about finding items that are both functional and aesthetically pleasing. Several editors mention shopping at luxury brands like Chanel Beauty, where they can find high-quality products that are also effective. Gift sets from these brands often arrive in reusable pouches, making them a practical choice as well. One editor notes that unique fragrances can make for great gifts, especially if they're not commonly known. Guerlain's 2026 debut is mentioned as an example of a lesser-known scent that can be appreciated by those who receive it. When it comes to luxury items, editors suggest gifting high-quality accessories like leather toiletry bags or wine carriers. Brands like Etoile and Freja offer stylish options for these types of gifts. In addition to beauty products and accessories, some editors are also thinking about functional gifts that can be used in various settings. For example, a scooter is mentioned as a great gift for children who have just learned how to ride one. Gifting luxury items doesn't have to mean breaking the bank. Editors suggest looking for brands that offer high-quality products at more affordable price points. This approach allows givers to splurge on special occasions without overspending. Overall, it seems that Vogue editors are putting thought and care into their gift choices this holiday season. Whether they're opting for luxury beauty products or practical accessories, each item is carefully selected with the recipient in mind. The art of gifting is all about showing you care and putting thought into every item chosen. Whether it's a luxurious beauty product or a practical accessory, each present should be tailored to the recipient's unique tastes and preferences. For those who appreciate the finer things in life, a relatively ordinary item with an especially lovely or personalized design can make all the difference. An everyday object transformed by its design becomes a thing of beauty that brings joy to the recipient's daily life. A beautifully designed journal is perfect for writers and planners, while a custom book stamp caters specifically to book lovers. For friends who are always on-the-go, a compact yet elegant mini brush is a thoughtful gift that won't get lost in their handbag. In addition to these lovely items, a whimsical lemon squeezer adds a touch of personality to any kitchen or home decor. A gorgeous lipstick case or sleek nail polish trio makes for an exceptional gift for the glamorous friend or family member. This year's holiday shopping season seems to be all about adding a touch of whimsy and personality to gifts. A beautiful bouquet of flowers can be elevated by pairing it with an eclectic vase that speaks to the recipient's unique style. Jonathan Adler's latest collection offers a range of fun and playful options for those who want to add some visual interest to their gift-giving. His designs are perfect for adding a pop of color and personality to any room, making them a great choice for the holidays. For wine enthusiasts, there's no better way to elevate their favorite bottle than with some stylish glassware or a clever bottle holder. These small touches can make all the difference in creating a special gift that shows thought and consideration. Finding the perfect gift can be a challenge, but one commerce producer has it down to a science. Fred Sahai admits that he gets too excited about giving gifts, often struggling to keep them under wraps until the big day. Coming from a household of girls, Sahai has an advantage when it comes to finding gifts for his loved ones. He can easily spot items that he and his sisters would all love, making gift-giving a breeze. One of his best beauty discoveries this year is Celisse's nail products, which have left him impressed with their quick-drying formula and long-lasting finish. His go-to brand for the holidays will undoubtedly be Celisse, with its high-quality polishes that dry in seconds without chipping. For those with coffee-loving dads or family members, an espresso cup collection is a thoughtful gift idea. Sahai continues to add new pieces to his dad's collection, showing how much thought and consideration can go into choosing the perfect present. The perfect gift is one that serves a purpose while also being stylish and chic. For those who know me well, they'll understand why I'm particularly fond of Barefaced's newly launched Discovery Kit, it's an excellent way to introduce friends and family to the brand. When it comes to tech-savvy individuals, a clever gift can make all the difference. Brick's innovative products have caught my attention, and I think their items would be an ideal stocking stuffer for those who are glued to their phones. As a lover of practical yet stylish gifts, I've often found myself recommending items that cater to both needs. Cozy winter accessories like sleek leather gloves from Agnelle or plush slippers from Ugg are always a hit during the holiday season. A beautifully designed coffee-table book is another gift idea that never fails to impress. The latest release dedicated to legendary fashion icon Grace Coddington is sure to delight any fashion enthusiast, and its festive theme makes it perfect for the holiday season. In addition to these thoughtful gifts, I've also been drawn to luxurious self-care items like beautifully scented bath oils, they're a lovely way to pamper oneself or show love and appreciation for someone special. articles.title: Haitians Support El Salvador's President Bukele Amid Gang Violence
articles.summary: Thousands of Haitians took to the streets on Tuesday to show support for El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele and his troops who have been battling gangs in Haiti.
articles.content: Thousands of Haitians took to the streets in Port-au-Prince and other parts of the country on Tuesday, showing their support for El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele and his troops who have been battling gangs in Haiti. The demonstrations were a display of gratitude towards the Central American leader and his military personnel, who have been deployed in Haiti since last month. During this time, Bukele's troops have targeted areas controlled by powerful gangs using explosive drones and robot dogs. The Haitian people are eager for relief from the violence that has plagued their country. The enthusiastic crowd waved Haitian flags and held up signs praising Bukele. Some demonstrators were heard shouting slogans such as "Bukele is here to free us!" while others yelled "Give them the drones and the dogs!" in reference to the military equipment being used against gangs. The deployment of 2,500 troops by El Salvador's president came after four of his soldiers went missing on October 18. Since then, fighting between gangs and foreign forces backed by Haitian authorities has intensified, with over 20,000 people killed in Haiti in the past five years. Experts warn that this surge of support for Bukele and his troops may not be sustainable once they withdraw from the country. Analysts like Diego Da Rin, who works with International Crisis Group, believe there's no long-term plan to keep Haiti safe after the Central American troops leave. The international community has been sounding the alarm about Haiti's fragile security situation for weeks, and a new report sheds light on the government's failure to develop a long-term plan to keep the country safe once foreign troops leave. A recent analysis based on over 100 interviews with officials in Haiti and abroad highlights the lack of strategy in addressing the gang problem. According to the report, the goal of the current foreign mission is not to dismantle gangs but to weaken them temporarily, leaving authorities vulnerable when international forces depart. The security situation in Haiti is complex, with various groups fighting against gangs, including Haitian police and soldiers, a U.N.-backed force, self-appointed vigilantes, and private security firms like Vectus Global. The latter was founded by Erik Prince, a former U.S. Navy SEAL and Blackwater founder, who has been involved in the firm's operations. The 2,500 Salvadoran troops currently deployed to Haiti are fighting against gangs that have taken control of significant areas of the country, including deep into gang-controlled territory. Their presence is part of an effort to provide temporary relief from the grip of these violent groups. A recent cartoon published in Le Nouvelliste newspaper captures the sentiment among Haitians who are cheering on President Bukele and his troops for their efforts against gangs, with a makeshift plan scribbled on a piece of paper labeled "PLAN ANTI GANG in colorful crayons. A significant gap exists between the number of police officers and the country's population size, as revealed by recent reports. With nearly 12 million people living in Haiti, the National Police force has a maximum of around 8,000 active officers. Some former government officials have expressed concerns that intelligence gathering would be overseen by a proposed National Security Council. This council was intended to develop a long-term strategy for making Haiti safer, but its establishment two years ago never materialized. Foreign donors are providing funding for various police units in Haiti, leading to different operational guidelines being followed depending on their benefactors. A foreign adviser has stated that the lack of a national strategy is causing this issue. The training period for new police officers was reduced from seven months to less than four, allowing more officers to be quickly deployed onto the streets. However, many of these officers occupy administrative positions rather than actively policing the country. The deployment of Salvadoran troops and equipment to Haiti has sparked mixed reactions among locals, with some expressing gratitude for the swift intervention while others remain skeptical about its effectiveness in addressing the country's deep-seated security issues. Cliford Vital, a resident of Port-au-Prince who lives in an area controlled by gangs, believes that President Bukele's decision to send troops and helicopters has brought about a significant shift in the balance of power. According to Vital, the presence of foreign forces has helped to reduce fear among residents, with many now feeling more secure than they did under previous leadership. However, experts at the International Crisis Group warn that relying on military might alone may not be enough to tackle Haiti's complex security challenges. They point out that the use of explosive drones and helicopters has yielded diminishing returns, failing to produce meaningful changes in territorial control or alter the balance of power on the ground. The report also highlights concerns about the lack of specialized training and equipment for Haitian security forces, which are often forced to rely on inadequate resources. Without a clear promotion system based on performance rather than politics, many officers occupy administrative positions rather than actively policing the country, exacerbating the problem. As foreign forces continue to play a significant role in Haiti's security landscape, concerns about civilian casualties and human rights abuses remain. The use of military might is expected to escalate further, potentially leading to an increase in civilian casualties as foreign forces increasingly rely on helicopters and explosive drones to target gangs. Haiti's Justice Minister Patrick Pélissier is expected to meet behind closed doors with Salvadoran officials during his visit to El Salvador for an international conference. According to reports, a bilateral agreement between Haiti and El Salvador would not be made public, despite concerns about the use of drones in the conflict against gangs. Salvadoran Vice President Félix Ulloa dismissed criticism, stating that there is a hidden agenda" behind the scrutiny of their operation. He maintained that respect for human rights and the rule of law was guaranteed under the agreement. The Salvadoran soldiers are expected to return home once four missing aviation technicians are found; meanwhile, efforts continue to establish a genuine rule of law in Haiti, enabling its institutions to function effectively. The passion and enthusiasm of the fans are palpable, making each premiere a truly special event. The premieres have been a whirlwind experience, with Zada struggling to keep up with the pace. Each stop has left its own unique impression on him, but he's particularly fond of the events in London and Mexico. In London, he got to spend quality time with his sister and her girlfriend, making the experience even more enjoyable. The event in Mexico was undoubtedly one of the highlights for Zada. The sheer number of fans in attendance was staggering, with thousands turning out to show their support. Despite the chaos, the reception was incredibly warm and welcoming. It's clear that Zada is still getting used to being a movie star, but he's soaking up every moment. As he prepares to attend another premiere, Zada's thoughts turn to his outfit for the evening. He's chosen a custom Louis Vuitton suit, designed in collaboration with Jason Bolden, and is particularly excited about the boots that will complement it perfectly. When asked about his look, Zada is eager to share the details. The boots are indeed eye-catching, and Zada is quick to acknowledge their style credentials. He's clearly a fan of the design, which adds a touch of glamour to an already impressive wardrobe. As he prepares to take on the red carpet once again, it's clear that Zada is ready to make a statement with his fashion choices. With each premiere, Zada is becoming more comfortable in his role as a movie star. The experience is still new and exciting for him, but he's learning to navigate the chaos and enjoy every moment of it. As he takes on the next stop on the promotional tour, it will be interesting to see how he continues to grow and adapt to the demands of fame. As Joseph Zada navigates his rise to fame, he's finding a newfound comfort in his wardrobe choices. The actor credits his stylist, Jason, with helping him find clothes that make him feel confident and at ease. articles.title: Saudi Arabia: Rights groups raise alarm over rising number of executions

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Executes Two Men for Terrorist Offenses
articles.summary: Two men were put to death in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province on Saturday.
articles.content: Saudi Arabia's alarming rate of executions continues to raise concerns among human rights groups worldwide. On Saturday, Jawad Abdullah Qureiris and Fadel Hassan al-Safwani were put to death in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. According to the Saudi authorities, both men had been convicted of terrorist offenses. The case of al-Safwani is particularly noteworthy, as he was a prominent organizer of peaceful protests calling for civil rights and the release of detainees back in 2011. At that time, Qureiris, who was still a minor, attended one of these protests in the city of Qatif. His involvement in this protest would later become a key factor in his arrest and detention. The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention had previously called for Qureiris' release in November 2024, deeming his detention arbitrary. This opinion also covered four other men, but Qureiris was the fourth of these five to be executed. Yousef al-Manasif, the fifth man, remains at risk after Saudi Arabia's Supreme Court upheld his death sentence. The two executions bring the total number of people put to death in Saudi Arabia this year to 211, according to an AFP tally reported on Monday. This tally includes 126 individuals convicted of drug trafficking and 17 people executed for terrorism-related charges. A significant proportion of those executed were foreign nationals: out of the 211 people, 100 were Saudi citizens. In recent months, Saudi authorities have been carrying out a series of executions that have raised eyebrows among human rights organizations. In July, five Ethiopian migrants were put to death for nonviolent drug-related offenses. Rights groups had also condemned the execution of two Bangladeshi nationals in October. The trend of executions continues unabated, with another Saudi national, Hassan Zaki al-Faraj, being executed on October 17 for alleged offenses committed when he was still a minor. The number of executions carried out by Saudi Arabia has reached alarming levels, according to human rights groups. In 2025, a record high of at least 356 people lost their lives in this manner, and the trend shows no signs of slowing down. Human Rights Watch's MENA spokesperson, Ahmed Benchemsi, confirms that over 2,000 individuals have been executed in Saudi Arabia during the past decade. This staggering figure puts the country third on a global list of executioners, behind only China and Iran. The Death Penalty Information Center provides further insight into the prevalence of executions worldwide. While comprehensive data for 2026 is not yet available, existing statistics suggest that Saudi Arabia's ranking as one of the world's top executioners is consistent with previous findings from Amnesty International. In many cases, death sentences in Saudi Arabia are issued under discretionary rulings known as ta'zir. This means that neither the crime nor the punishment is defined by Islamic law, or Sharia, as interpreted by the Saudi government. As a result, little information is provided about the execution or the fate of the bodies involved. The ongoing conflict between Saudi Arabia and its regional adversaries has added to the country's woes. Following the US-Israeli attacks on Iran in February, Riyadh has faced retaliatory strikes from both Iran and the Houthi group in Yemen, resulting in significant loss of life and damage to infrastructure. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is now facing a daunting challenge as he navigates these complex regional dynamics while also implementing his Vision 2030 reform plan. Several high-profile events have had to be canceled or postponed due to the ongoing security threats, further straining Riyadh's efforts to diversify its economy and boost international investment. The Saudi government's inability to protect its population from repeated Houthi attacks on its airports has exposed a vulnerability in the country despite record-breaking defense spending levels. This weakness is being exploited by rights groups who argue that the government is using the ongoing war as an excuse to intensify its crackdown on dissent. One of the most disturbing consequences of this crackdown is the relentless pace of executions and corporal punishment sentences, according to human rights lawyer Sarah Lea Whitson. Watchdogs have reported a number of cases in recent weeks, including that of a Kenyan woman who was sentenced to 100 lashes for giving birth outside marriage. This sentence has sparked widespread outrage among human rights groups, who argue that it is a clear indication of the Saudi government's reliance on brute repression to rule the country. The use of corporal punishment as a tool of state control is not unique to this case, however. Human rights organizations have long criticized the Saudi government for its treatment of migrant workers, who are often subjected to harsh punishments for minor infractions. Maryam Aldossari, acting director of the London-based human rights organization ALQST, argues that the war in Iran and wider regional tensions have provided the perfect cover for the Saudi authorities to intensify their crackdown on dissent. This has resulted in an increased use of the death penalty as a tool of political repression against the country's Shia minority. The predominantly Sunni population of Saudi Arabia often views its Shia minority with suspicion, partly due to concerns over Iranian influence and alleged links between domestic dissent and Tehran. These accusations have been used by rights groups to justify repression of the minority, which is concentrated in the oil-rich Eastern Province where many of the recently executed men hailed from. The introduction of social reforms in Saudi Arabia over the past decade, aimed at expanding opportunities for women while maintaining control over political dissent and activism, suggests that the kingdom's human rights environment is complex and multifaceted. According to Neil Quilliam, associate fellow in the Middle East and North Africa Programme at Chatham House, regional tensions can heighten official concern about national security, leading to reduced tolerance for public criticism or perceived threats to social cohesion. This could potentially lead to a more constrained space for dissent, not only in Saudi Arabia but also in other Gulf states. The Riyadh airport attack has raised questions about the future of human rights in Saudi Arabia, with some observers suggesting that regional tensions are exacerbating concerns about national security and limiting room for public criticism. The introduction of social reforms is seen as a double-edged sword, offering new opportunities while maintaining strict controls over dissent and activism. The Human Rights Commission in Saudi Arabia has yet to respond to DW's inquiry on the matter, leaving many questions unanswered. Despite this lack of clarity, it is clear that the human rights situation in Saudi Arabia remains a pressing concern for observers around the world.
